Split pane

Source: R/widget-split.R
split_pane.Rd

Two panes separated by a divider the user can drag with the mouse (press on the divider, move, release) or move with the keyboard (focus the divider with Tab; arrows move it, Shift+arrows ten cells, Home / End to the ends). Typical uses: a tree next to a preview, a table above a detail view, an editor above its output.

Usage

split_pane(
  first,
  second,
  direction = "horizontal",
  ratio = 0.5,
  min_size = 3L,
  id = NULL,
  classes = NULL,
  style = NULL
)

Arguments

first, second

The two panes.

direction

"horizontal": panes side by side, divider vertical; "vertical": stacked panes.

ratio

Share of the first pane, between 0 and 1.

min_size

Smallest pane size in cells.

id

Optional identifier.

classes

Optional classes.

style

A style().

Value

A SplitPane widget with $ratio and $sizes.

Details

The panes fill their share of the space regardless of their own size styles. ratio is the share of the first pane; min_size keeps both panes from collapsing. The pane sends "splitpane.resized" (ratio) when the user finishes moving the divider. Experimental.

Examples

ui <- split_pane(label("left"), label("right"), ratio = 0.4)
render_widget(ui, 20, 2)$to_text()
#> [1] "left    │right      " "        │           "
